children: , the enterprise-technology and hybrid-cloud heavyweight, launched an open-source AI model with NASA Thursday to help scientists read the Moon's surface more precisely. The shares slipped approximately 0.8% to $238.14 during morning trading. According to Reuters, the model learned from more than 30 synchronized data layers gathered by nine instruments across four missions.

The numbers give the project real weight. IBM said the system mapped critical lunar features with up to 23% greater accuracy than established techniques, cut potential ice-location errors by as much as 22% and improved broader crater detection by nearly 19%. It achieved those results using only half as much training data. Better maps could help mission planners choose landing zones, locate resources and reduce uncertainty before expensive equipment ever leaves Earth.

The immediate business payoff remains less obvious because NASA is releasing the model, data and code for public use. Still, IBM gains a powerful showcase for applying its foundation-model technology far beyond conventional corporate workloads. The chart adds a modest valuation signal: IBM's $238.14 share price sits 1.83% below its $242.57 GF Value estimate. The discount is small, so the bigger question is whether IBM can turn scientific credibility into paid cloud, consulting and enterprise-AI contracts.

title: IBM Falls While Its Moon AI Scores 23% Better
